case_title: RAMVIR v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of Section 149, convicted under Section 302
high_court_outcome: Upheld conviction under Section 302 and convicted under Sections 148/149
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused, along with five other individuals, surrounded the victim and his son and fired shots, resulting in the victim's death. The accused and the five others were initially tried for offenses under Sections 148 and 149 of the IPC, along with Section 302. The trial court acquitted the five co-accused of the charges under Sections 148 and 149 but convicted the accused under Section 302. The High Court upheld the conviction under Section 302 and further convicted the accused under Sections 148 and 149. The Supreme Court, however, found the conviction under Sections 148 and 149 not legally sustainable, as the accused had already been acquitted by the trial court, and the High Court was not justified in convicting him under those sections. The Court also found the conviction under Section 302 not factually and legally sustainable due to lack of evidence linking the accused to the fatal shot and issues with the ballistic report.
